## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change removes the self-exit behind #12225. A screensaver that is not the active window at its first focus poll no longer closes itself, so the idle service no longer treats it as a dismissal and the pending lock stays armed. Keypress dismissal, dismissal on focus loss after first focus, and the lock path behave as before. The new `BASH_SOURCE` guard does not affect any launch path in the repository (all terminal `-e` launches and the `bash -lc` fallback execute the script directly). The new test fails on base and passes on head.

One behavior trade-off is worth handling, plus an optional test improvement.

### A screensaver that never receives focus now stays up with no bound

`screensaver_lost_focus` returns false on every poll until the screensaver has been the active window once ([`bin/omarchy-screensaver#L14-L20`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/89b4f538c43239151fb6461982e4ed9524b95162/bin/omarchy-screensaver#L14-L20)). If Hyprland never focuses it, nothing in the watchdog ends it. Hyprland 0.56.2 withholds initial focus from a newly mapped window when an interactive layer holds keyboard focus (Omarchy's menu, clipboard, emoji picker, polkit prompt and reminder overlays), when the focused surface has an active pointer constraint, or when a `stay_focused` window is visible ([`Window.cpp#L2425-L2458`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/desktop/view/Window.cpp#L2425-L2458), [`FocusState.cpp#L109-L112`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/desktop/state/FocusState.cpp#L109-L112)). In the overlay case the map-time fullscreen rule is skipped too ([`Window.cpp#L2473-L2490`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/desktop/view/Window.cpp#L2473-L2490)), and closing the overlay refocuses the previously focused window, not the screensaver.

```text
Screensaver never becomes the active window
                    base                           head
watchdog            exits on first poll (~1 s)     keeps polling, no exit
keypress            goes to the focused surface    goes to the focused surface
idle-cycle launch   cycle cancelled, no lock       lock fires at its deadline
manual launch       flashes and vanishes           stays up until focused or locked
```

The table is from source review of Hyprland 0.56.2 and Omarchy, plus stubbed runs of the watchdog loop (stub `hyprctl` returning a non-screensaver class). The focus-withholding cases were not reproduced in a live compositor.

**Impact:** in an idle cycle, the idle service ignores activity while a screensaver window exists ([`Service.qml#L158-L171`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/89b4f538c43239151fb6461982e4ed9524b95162/shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml#L158-L171)), so a user who returns and types into the focused app is still locked at the deadline. A manual launch (System menu > Screensaver, branding previews, CLI) has no lock timer, so while the user keeps working the unfocused screensaver stays up until it is hovered or clicked and then dismissed, or the session is locked. While it exists, further launches silently do nothing ([`omarchy-launch-screensaver#L6`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/89b4f538c43239151fb6461982e4ed9524b95162/bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver#L6)). Omarchy's own menu path normally unmaps its overlay before the screensaver maps, so the manual case needs an extra condition such as a user keybind over an overlay or a pointer-locking app.

**Suggested change:** bound the pre-focus state instead of waiting indefinitely. Optional approaches: exit after a few seconds without first focus only when the screensaver was not launched by an idle cycle (the idle service already tracks that with `screensaverStartedThisCycle`), or have the idle service keep the lock armed when a never-focused screensaver closes. Either keeps the #12225 fix on the idle path. Neither approach was tested.

**Note on the stated cause:** in Hyprland 0.56.2 the `openwindow` event and initial focus happen in the same synchronous map handler ([`Window.cpp#L2366-L2371`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/desktop/view/Window.cpp#L2366-L2371)), so a later `hyprctl activewindow` poll cannot land "before Hyprland has focused the new window". The failing cycles in #12225 are more consistent with focus being withheld or taken at map, which is the case above. The fix does not depend on the explanation, but the code comment could say "the screensaver may not be the active window when the first poll runs".

**Optional test improvement:** the only check on the watchdog loop is a negative `rg` for the exact old line. In mutation runs, the test still passed with the loop changed to `if read -n1 -t 1; then` (focus ignored entirely) and with the old condition restored as `read -t 1 -n1 || ! screensaver_in_focus`. A positive assertion that the loop condition calls `screensaver_lost_focus`, or moving the loop decision into a small function tested with the existing stub, would catch both. Adding `require_command rg` would also stop the negative check from passing when `rg` is missing.
